problem: A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis under the action of a force of magnitude $2{x}^{2}\,\text{N}$ acting in the direction of increasing $x.$ Given that $x$ is measured in meters, calculate the work done by the force in moving the particle from $x=0$ to $x=1.$
worked_solution:
The work done by a force $F=F(x)$ in moving a particle from $x={x}_{1}$ to $x={x}_{2}$ is given by

$$
W={\int }_{{x}_{1}}^{{x}_{2}}F(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

When the force and distance are measured in Newtons and meters, respectively, the work done by the force is measured in Joules ($J$).

Substituting the given values into our integral, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}W & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{3}{x}^{3}{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(1-0) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\,J.\end{aligned}
$$
